transcript.text: Good evening, everyone. Let's get started. We've got the talent-show finale going live this Saturday at 9:00 PM Eastern, and we need to finalize the voting package tonight so we can get through the pre-air lock meeting with standards, platform production, rights, and data protection. The current draft has SMS and online portal voting open to our broadcast audience. Before I make the binding call on the final package, I want to hear from each of you — what issues, risks, or gaps do you see with the voting setup as it stands? Let's go around the room.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something critical. After the draft voting rules were circulated, I issued the network's current standards memo, which sets binding requirements: voters must be at least 13 years old, each voter may cast exactly one vote per verified account, and voting must close at 9:50 PM Eastern. The current draft voting package doesn't reflect these requirements, and they need to be incorporated before we finalize tonight.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share critical findings from this morning's platform certification test. The SMS integration failed certification — it is not approved for use. The web portal passed certification, but there's an important requirement: the approved portal requires account verification before a vote is accepted. This means our current draft, which lists both SMS and online portal voting, cannot go forward as written. SMS must be removed, and the portal's account verification requirement needs to be reflected in the final voting package.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical rights issue. I obtained the finalist label's written approval today. The approval confirms that the voting interface may display finalist names and approved headshots, but it may NOT use any finalist performance audio or video. The problem is that the current draft voting interface still contains performance clips. Those clips must be removed before we finalize, or we'll be broadcasting without the necessary rights clearance.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical data protection issue. My privacy review with the voting vendor, completed this week, establishes two binding requirements: first, participation must be limited to viewers physically located in the United States and Canada — the current draft still describes worldwide participation, which is not permitted. Second, voter identifiers must be deleted within 30 days — the current draft has no deletion step at all. Both of these gaps need to be corrected in the final voting package before we finalize tonight.
transcript.speaker: A5

transcript.text:
Thank you all for those critical flags. Let me make sure I have everything straight before I make the binding decision.

Julian: Standards requires minimum voter age of 13, exactly one vote per verified account, and voting closes at 9:50 PM Eastern. The current draft doesn't reflect these.

Nia: SMS failed platform certification and must be removed. The web portal passed but requires account verification before a vote is accepted.

Leon: We have the label's written approval for finalist names and headshots only — no performance audio or video. The current draft still has performance clips that must be removed.

Sofia: Data protection requires participation limited to viewers in the US and Canada only — the draft currently says worldwide. And voter identifiers must be deleted within 30 days — the draft has no deletion step.

So the final package needs to incorporate all of these: online portal only with account verification, age 13 minimum, one vote per verified account, voting closes 9:50 PM Eastern, US and Canada only, finalist names and headshots only with no performance clips, and 30-day voter identifier deletion.

Before I settle, does anyone have anything else to add or any concerns about how these requirements interact? For instance, are there any conflicts between the standards requirements and the platform or data protection requirements that we need to reconcile?

transcript.text: Mara, I've reviewed the requirements from all four areas and I don't see any conflicts — they're complementary. To walk through the interactions: My standards memo requires account verification for one-vote-per-account, and Nia's platform certification independently requires account verification before accepting a vote — so those two requirements reinforce each other rather than conflict. The age-13 minimum and one-vote-per-verified-account rules work cleanly through the verified portal since verification can confirm both identity and age eligibility. The 9:50 PM Eastern close time gives us a clean 50-minute voting window within the live broadcast. Sofia's US-and-Canada geographic restriction and 30-day deletion requirement are independent controls that layer on top without interfering with the voting mechanics. And Leon's rights clearance — names and headshots only, no performance clips — is purely about what the voting interface displays, which doesn't interact with the voting mechanics at all. So the final package is internally consistent: online portal only, account verified, age 13+, one vote per account, US/Canada only, closes 9:50 PM Eastern, names and headshots only, 30-day identifier deletion. No reconciliation needed between any of the requirements.
